newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weak dollar weighs on German shares, Daimler down.
newsitem.headline: Weak dollar weighs on German shares, Daimler down.

text.p: The dollar's decline against the mark put pressure on German shares in early trade on Monday, with export-driven Daimler-Benz AG getting a double hit over fears of higher petrol prices.
Daimler led trading volumes and suffered the second biggest losses in pre-bourse trade to decline 2.90 marks, or more than two percent, to 127.50 marks by 0747 GMT.
The blue chip IBIS DAX index of electronic trade was down 39.03 points, or 1.2 percent, at 3,322.17 points while June DTB DAX futures were down 44 points at 3,328.0.
Weak Bunds also helped depress the share market.

After a weak start, Bunds continued to tick lower after March M3 money supply came in as expected at an annualised rate of 8.3 percent. Economists noted that the underlying reasons for the rate reaffirmed muted expectations for a German economic recovery.
Daimler's strong decline followed a report in Germany's mass circulation Bild newspaper which said the government planned a sharp increase in petrol tax before the summer.
But dealers also noted that the share had fallen below a technically important level of 130 marks, and was thus likely to recover its ground again in the short term.
Other car shares were also under pressure with BMW down 29 marks, or about two percent at 1,360 marks while Volkswagen AG, in line with the market trend, was down 9.50 marks at 1,063 marks.
With little other crucial economic and corporate news expected, activity was expected to be thin for the rest of the day.
The few outperformers included the ever-volatile software group SAP AG, whose preferred stock was up 1.3 percent at 289 marks ahead of the company's quarterly earnings report due Tuesday.
On the broader market, dealers said 3,300 DAX points remained a key psychological support level for the market. Below that, support was pegged at around 3,260, dealers said.
